title: Check every figure and test a loan before you sign

say: Check every figure, and test a loan before you sign.
This is the video for module 2 of Accessing Grants, Loans and Partnerships.
Applications fail for boring reasons far more often than big ones: a missing document, a form submitted an hour after the portal closed.

say: And a loan is only good if your business can repay it from normal cash flow, without borrowing again or taking money meant for the family. Today you learn to check all of this yourself.

say: Put three sources side by side: what you wrote, your records, and your bank statements. They should tell the same story.
Chioma's application says her sales are about 1,800,000 naira a month.
Her six months of statements show 7,200,000 naira in total, which is 1,200,000 a month. A gap of 600,000.
Her records explain most of it. About 500,000 naira a month is paid in cash and spent on ajo and stock before it reaches the bank. The rest came from using a festive month as an average.
So she corrects her figure to 1,700,000 naira and attaches a note with her sales book.
Never inflate figures or edit a statement. It is dishonest, changing a financial document can be forgery, and banks check.
For example, Grace sells frozen fish and chicken in Ibadan. She wants 500,000 naira for six months, and two lenders both quote 3% a month. Always ask for the full repayment schedule in writing.
Lender A charges a flat rate: interest on the full 500,000 every month. That is 90,000 naira. It also takes a 2% fee upfront, so she receives 490,000 but repays 590,000. A true cost of 100,000 naira.

panel.heading: Grace compares two ₦500,000 loans
left: Interest on full amount every month
right: Interest only on what is still owed

say: Lender B uses a reducing balance: interest only on what she still owes. That is about 53,800 naira, plus a 1% fee. A true cost of about 58,800 naira.
Both said 3% a month, but Lender A costs her about 41,200 naira more.

panel.heading: Grace compares two ₦500,000 loans
left: Interest on full amount every month
right: Interest only on what is still owed

say: Now the most important test. Free cash is money in, minus business costs, minus what you take home for the family. Lender B's payment is about 92,300 naira a month.
In an average month Grace has about 150,000 naira free, so 57,700 is left.

cards.d: Free cash about ₦150,000. After the repayment, ₦57,700 is left.
Free cash about ₦85,000. After the repayment, she is ₦7,300 short.
Hold back a reserve of one month's payment, ask for a longer term, or borrow less.

say: But in her slowest month she had only about 85,000 naira. She would be 7,300 short.

say: So before signing, she holds back a reserve of one month's payment, or asks for a longer term, or borrows less. And she does not count the freezer's extra profit until it shows in her records.

say: Before you sign any loan, write down the total repayable, every fee, the dates, and the late penalty.
Know what happens to collateral or a guarantor if you default. A guarantor can be asked to repay for you, and late payments go to credit bureaus. Only sign when the bad-month test passes.

panel.heading: Write these down in plain words
items: Total amount repayable
Every fee
Repayment dates
Penalty for late payment
What happens to collateral or guarantor
Can you repay early without charge?

say: To remember. Follow the six stages and submit early. Make your application, records and statements agree, and explain any honest difference.
Never inflate or edit documents. A flat rate costs far more than a reducing balance. And test every loan against your worst month.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Six stages; submit at least two days early
Application, records and statements must agree
Never inflate, invent or edit documents
Flat rate costs far more than reducing
Test the loan against your worst month
